xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4951: Agent MCP and bots (W-BOT1): "Connect a bot" in Settings → Anywhere

plan.title: Agent MCP and bots (W-BOT1): "Connect a bot" in Settings → Anywhere
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Outside bots (Hermes, OpenClaw, Grok Build, Grok Bot, the xAI API) need a way to get scoped, revocable access to this machine, but Settings → Anywhere only offers Copy MCP URL with operate-level defaults and no per-platform setup.
narratives.Proposal: A frontend-only 'Connect a bot' dialog (opened from a new Bots panel and the command palette) that picks a platform, a reach (Overdeck connector, Tailscale, This computer, Public MCP) and bot scopes (default read:state, read:conversations, tell; read:state locked on), then mints a connector pairing string (POST /api/connectors/pairing) or an access token (POST /api/access-tokens, clamped to the five bot scopes) or shows public MCP setup, plus the exact platform config from pure snippet functions in botSnippets.ts. Full spec: .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No server route, route-scopes row or no-loss-matrix row is added or changed.
- No connector process, OAuth server, public MCP switch/panel, approval card or integration package (W-CONN2, W-OAUTH1/2, W-FUN1, W-INT1..4).
- No configuration/bots.mdx and no docs.json change (W-DOC, PAN-4958).
- Config snippets never contain token text; only the once-shown 'Token setup' field may.
- The dialog never sends admin, forward, read:settings, read:costs or read:events.
- No QR code for the pairing string.
- No change to the Access tokens or Devices panels.
- MCP_DEFAULT_SCOPES in anywhereApi.ts is not reused or changed.

autoDecisions.summary: botSnippets.ts and the PRD's 'Snippet text' are the reference; the not-yet-written W-INT READMEs must match them.
autoDecisions.rationale: No integration README exists yet; the epic PRD already fixes the README text, which the PRD quotes verbatim, so AC-23 is checkable now.

autoDecisions.summary: Config snippets use env placeholders; the token appears only in a once-shown 'Token setup' field.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the README text (${OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN}) and is stricter than the epic's test sentence, keeping tokens out of config files (epic NFR-2).

autoDecisions.summary: read:state is locked on; read:conversations and tell are default-on but can be unticked.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-4949 D-14 says the dialog shows read:state as always on; AC-23 and FR-14 call the others defaults.

autoDecisions.summary: Scopes are clamped client-side to the five bot scopes for both reaches.
autoDecisions.rationale: POST /api/access-tokens accepts any scope, so the dialog must enforce epic NFR-11 itself.

autoDecisions.summary: Public MCP reach treats a 404 from GET /api/mcp/public as 'off'.
autoDecisions.rationale: W-FUN1 (PAN-4947) has not landed; the dialog ships complete and lights up when it does.

autoDecisions.summary: Single form with three numbered sections instead of a Next/Back wizard.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches McpUrlDialog, fewer states and simpler tests while still presenting the PRD's three steps.

autoDecisions.summary: Add a 'Connect a bot' command-palette row alongside the store/host entry.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD adds 'connect-bot' to the dialog store; a host entry without the palette opener would be half-done.

autoDecisions.summary: Docs go into the existing configuration/mcp.mdx as a 'Connect a bot' section.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids colliding with W-DOC (PAN-4958), which creates configuration/bots.mdx and edits docs.json.

items.title: Add the pure bot snippet module botSnippets.ts

narrative.Action: Implement every constant and function in the PRD section 'Snippet text' (.pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md) exactly, in new botSnippets.ts (<=250 lines): CONNECTOR_LOCAL_URL, TAILSCALE_PLACEHOLDER_ORIGIN, PUBLIC_MCP_PLACEHOLDER_URL, XAI_ALLOWED_TOOLS, BotPlatform, BotReach, OauthLevel, BOT_PLATFORMS, REACH_LABELS, defaultBotName, shellQuote, hermesConfig, openclawConfig, grokBuildMcpJson, grokBotMcpJson, xaiExample, oauthIssueCommand, oauthLevelForScopes, connectorCommands, tokenSetup. Only tokenSetup may emit token text; config snippets use ${OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN} / ${OVERDECK_CONNECTOR_LOCAL_TOKEN} placeholders. Module header names PAN-4927 W-BOT1 (PAN-4951) and says the integration READMEs must match these functions. Add the test path to scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt in sorted position. Tests must not read source/doc files and must not skip.

items.title: Given hermesConfig({ reach: 'connector', url: CONNECTOR_LOCAL_URL }), it returns text containing 'http://127.0.0.1:7466/mcp' and 'Bearer ${OVERDECK_CONNECTOR_LOCAL_TOKEN}', and openclawConfig returns text containing 'transport: "streamable-http"'

grokBuildMcpJson() returns JSON whose mcpServers.overdeck.command equals '${GROK_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run-mcp.sh', and grokBotMcpJson({ url: 'https://box.tail1.ts.net:8443/mcp' }) returns JSON with exactly one server whose url ends in ':8443/mcp'
For every input in the test table, no function except tokenSetup returns text matching /od[krl]_/, and tokenSetup returns text containing the given token
oauthLevelForScopes returns 'approve', 'operate', 'message' and 'read' for the four D-8 cases, shellQuote("it's") returns 'it'\''s', and defaultBotName('grok-bot') returns 'Grok Bot'
Add botsApi.ts: connectors, pairing, public MCP and the scope clamp

narrative.Action: Create botsApi.ts (<=150 lines) exactly as WI-2 in .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md: BOTS_CONNECTORS_QUERY_KEY ['anywhere-connectors'], PUBLIC_MCP_QUERY_KEY ['anywhere-public-mcp'], BOT_SCOPE_CHOICES (read:state, read:conversations, tell, operate, approve), BotScope, BOT_DEFAULT_SCOPES (read:state, read:conversations, tell), botScopes(chosen) (filter to choices, always add read:state, choice order), ConnectorRow, BotsForbiddenError, loadConnectors (GET /api/connectors; 403 throws BotsForbiddenError), removeConnector (DELETE /api/connectors/:id), createConnectorPairing (POST /api/connectors/pairing with { name, scopes }), PublicMcpState and loadPublicMcp (GET /api/mcp/public; 404 maps to { available:false, enabled:false, url:null }; ok maps baseUrl to url). Keep a private readResult like directoryApi.ts; import apiError/isOk/ApiResult from anywhereApi.ts; mutations use dashboardMutationJsonHeaders(). Add the test path to scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt sorted.

items.title: botScopes(['tell', 'admin', 'forward']) returns ['read:state', 'tell'] and botScopes([]) returns ['read:state']

Given /api/mcp/public answers 404, loadPublicMcp resolves { available: false, enabled: false, url: null }; given { enabled: true, baseUrl: 'https://h.ts.net:8443/mcp' } it resolves { available: true, enabled: true, url: 'https://h.ts.net:8443/mcp' }
Given /api/connectors answers 403, loadConnectors rejects with BotsForbiddenError, and createConnectorPairing sends POST /api/connectors/pairing with JSON body { name, scopes }
Build ConnectBotDialog with the connector reach output

narrative.Action: Follow WI-3 in .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md. New ConnectBotDialog.tsx (<=300 lines): one form (D-5) with sections '1. Platform' (radios over BOT_PLATFORMS), '2. Reach' (only the platform's reaches, REACH_LABELS, reset on platform change), '3. Access' (five checkboxes in BOT_SCOPE_CHOICES order; read:state checked and disabled 'always on'; read:conversations and tell default on and tickable; operate 'can start and stop work' and approve 'can answer questions and permission prompts' default off; Grok Bot shows the FR-4 sentence instead), Name (default defaultBotName, maxLength 64, trimmed, empty disables the button). data-component='connect-bot-dialog', role='dialog', aria-labelledby='connect-bot-title', title 'Connect a bot'. For reach connector the button 'Create pairing code' calls createConnectorPairing(name.trim(), botScopes(scopes)); 403 renders 'Only a browser on this machine can connect bots.'; success invalidates BOTS_CONNECTORS_QUERY_KEY and shows ConnectBotOutput (new file, <=300 lines): CopyField 'Pairing string' + pairingExpiresInText(Date.parse(expiresAt)), CopyField multiline 'Connector commands' = connectorCommands({ version, pairingString, serve: platform !== 'grok-build' }) with version from loadEnvironment().serverVersion ('latest' until loaded), CopyField multiline '<label> config' (hermesConfig/openclawConfig with CONNECTOR_LOCAL_URL, or grokBuildMcpJson()), and a Done button. Export CopyField from McpUrlDialog.tsx by adding the export keyword only (D-14). Other reaches keep the action button disabled until the next items land. Add the test path to scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt sorted.

items.title: Given the default form, when 'Create pairing code' is clicked, then fetch receives POST /api/connectors/pairing whose body scopes are exactly ['read:state', 'read:conversations', 'tell'] and name is 'Hermes bot'; ticking approve first adds 'approve' to the body
The read:state checkbox renders checked and disabled, and unticking tell removes 'tell' from the pairing request body

Given a mocked pairing response, the dialog renders a pairing string that parseConnectorPairLink from @overdeck/contracts parses to a non-null value, and a 'Connector commands' field containing 'npx -y @overdeck/core@<serverVersion> mcp connector pair'
Given POST /api/connectors/pairing answers 403, the dialog renders 'Only a browser on this machine can connect bots.'
Add the Tailscale and This computer token reaches to the dialog

narrative.Action: Follow WI-4 in .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md. For reaches tailscale and this-computer the button is 'Create token' and calls createAccessToken(name.trim(), botScopes(scopes)) from anywhereApi.ts; success invalidates ANYWHERE_ACCESS_TOKENS_QUERY_KEY. Output: 'This token is shown once.', CopyField multiline 'Token setup' = tokenSetup({ platform, reach, token, origin }), CopyField multiline '<label> config' = hermesConfig({ reach: 'tailscale', url: origin + '/mcp' }) / openclawConfig(...) / grokBuildMcpJson(). origin = AnywhereStatus.tailscale.serveUrl without trailing slashes, else TAILSCALE_PLACEHOLDER_ORIGIN with the note 'Tailscale Serve is not set up on this machine yet. Set up Tailscale, then replace the placeholder.' (D-10). 403 renders the D-13 forbidden text.

items.title: Given platform Grok Build, the reach defaults to 'This computer', and 'Create token' sends POST /api/access-tokens whose body scopes are exactly ['read:state', 'read:conversations', 'tell']
Given a minted token, the 'Token setup' field contains the token text and the config field contains no odk_ text

Given Hermes with Tailscale and serveUrl 'https://box.tail1.ts.net', the config field renders 'url: "https://box.tail1.ts.net/mcp"'; given serveUrl null, it renders 'https://YOUR-MACHINE.YOUR-TAILNET.ts.net/mcp' and the D-10 note
Add the Public MCP reach for Grok Bot and the xAI API

narrative.Action: Follow WI-5 in .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md. For reach public, query loadPublicMcp (PUBLIC_MCP_QUERY_KEY). When enabled is false (a 404 included): text 'Public MCP is off. Hosted bots need it: turn it on under Public MCP in Settings → Anywhere.' and button 'Show Public MCP settings' that calls requestSettingsSection('anywhere'), closes the dialog, then document.querySelector('[data-component="public-mcp-panel"]')?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' }) (D-7); no create button. When enabled: button 'Show setup'. Output: CopyField 'Public MCP URL' = url ?? PUBLIC_MCP_PLACEHOLDER_URL (D-6 note when null). Grok Bot: CopyField multiline 'Grok Bot mcp.json' = grokBotMcpJson({ url }) plus 'Grok Bot signs in with OAuth on first use. Approve the sign-in in this dashboard and pick its access level there.' xAI API: CopyField 'Get a token' = oauthIssueCommand({ name: name.trim(), level: oauthLevelForScopes(botScopes(scopes)) }) and CopyField multiline 'xAI API example' = xaiExample({ url }). The dialog mints nothing for either platform.

items.title: Given platform Grok Bot, the Reach section renders only the 'Public MCP' option and no 'Overdeck connector' option
Given GET /api/mcp/public answers 404, the dialog renders 'Public MCP is off' and the 'Show Public MCP settings' button, and sends no POST request
Given { enabled: true, baseUrl: 'https://box.tail1.ts.net:8443/mcp' }, Grok Bot's mcp.json field contains that URL, and xAI API with operate ticked renders '--level operate'
For Grok Bot and xAI API, the dialog sends no request to /api/access-tokens or /api/connectors/pairing

narrative.Action: D-12 in .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md: add 'connect-bot' to the AnywhereDialog union; render <ConnectBotDialog open={dialog === 'connect-bot'} onClose={close} /> in AnywhereDialogHost; add a DIALOG_ROWS entry { id: 'anywhere-connect-bot', label: 'Connect a bot', icon: Bot (lucide-react), dialog: 'connect-bot', description: 'Give Hermes, OpenClaw or Grok access to this machine', keywords: ['anywhere', 'bot', 'mcp', 'hermes', 'openclaw', 'grok'] } after 'Set up Tailscale'; update the header comment count ('Six open' -> 'Seven open'). Update palette-anywhere-actions.test.ts (eight labels, new DIALOG_ROWS row, test title 'lists the eight Anywhere actions in order') and add a host test case.

The 'Connect a bot' palette action opens the dialog: selecting it calls openAnywhereDialog('connect-bot')

Add the Bots panel to Settings → Anywhere

narrative.Action: Follow WI-7 in .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md. New BotsPanel.tsx (<=150 lines), data-component='anywhere-bots-panel', heading 'Bots', useQuery({ queryKey: BOTS_CONNECTORS_QUERY_KEY, queryFn: loadConnectors, refetchInterval: 5000, retry: false }). States like AccessTokensPanel.tsx: 'Loading bots…'; BotsForbiddenError -> 'Only a browser on this machine can manage bots.' and no button; other errors 'Could not load bots: <message>'; empty 'No bots connected.'; rows with name, scopes joined by ', ', created and last used (formatRelativeTime), and Remove -> useConfirm({ title: 'Remove <name>?', message: 'The connector loses access at once.', confirmLabel: 'Remove', variant: 'destructive' }) -> removeConnector(id) -> toast.error on failure -> invalidate. A 'Connect a bot' button (unless forbidden) calls openAnywhereDialog('connect-bot'). Mount <BotsPanel /> in AnywhereSection.tsx directly after <AccessTokensPanel />. Add the test path to scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt sorted.

narrative.Action: Follow WI-8 in .pan/drafts/PAN-4951.md: add '## Connect a bot' after the '## Revoking' section of configuration/mcp.mdx with: where it is (Settings → Anywhere → Bots → Connect a bot, or the command palette); the platform → reach table (Hermes/OpenClaw: Overdeck connector (default) or Tailscale; Grok Build: This computer (default), Overdeck connector or Tailscale; Grok Bot/xAI API: Public MCP); access defaults (read:state always on; read:conversations and tell on; operate and approve off) and that bots never get admin, forward, read:settings or read:costs; what each reach produces (pairing string works once within 10 minutes plus npx -y @overdeck/core@<version> mcp connector login|pair|serve; access token shown once and kept out of config via OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN / OVERDECK_MCP_TOKEN_FILE; public URL and the pan mcp oauth issue command); the Hermes connector config block verbatim from 'Snippet text' §3; Remove in the Bots panel revokes a connector at once; the connector and public MCP commands arrive with PAN-4950 and PAN-4947.
